judged_text: Only evt.destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the booking (the Booking.destinationCalendar relation stays one-to-one), so the collected team destination calendars exist only in the in-memory evt and are lost on persistence. Flows that rebuild evt from the booking afterwards — booking confirmation (confirm.handler.ts:175) and payment success (webhook.ts:229, paypal-webhook.ts:152) — construct destinationCalendar with only the main host's calendar, so paid or confirmation-gated COLLECTIVE bookings get their calendar event created only in the main host's calendar and the other hosts' calendars never receive the event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, `handleNewBooking` collects additional team members’ `destinationCalendar`s into `teamDestinationCalendars` and pushes them onto `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the Booking, only the first destination calendar is connected: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (handleNewBooking.ts around the booking create input). Separately, later flows that rebuild `evt` from the stored booking (e.g., confirm.handler.ts and payment webhooks) set `destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) or `user.destinationCalendar`, wrapping it into a 1-element array, so they cannot recreate the team calendars. Given `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` to create multiple calendar events, these rebuilt `evt`s will only create an event for the main host calendar, dropping other hosts’ calendars in confirmation/payment-gated cases.
